# v0.29.0 — local semantic recall on by default, fuller recall and safer retries

v0.29.0 follows v0.28.1. This tree is the `v0.29.0-rc2` tag plus this notes file. The release gauntlet ran at that tag; its results and the release-manager decisions are under **Qualification**, with receipts attached to this release.

Local semantic recall is now on by default. Recall returns more exact matches from long messages and counts duplicate copies once. Retried and stopped turns are stored more reliably. Compaction stops redoing work that changed nothing. Three default-on additions write new data to the store; they are listed first below.

Session-pack recall and entity memory stay off by default. No answer-quality gain is claimed for this release.

## On by default in this release

- **Local semantic recall** (described under **Changes since v0.28.1**). On LongMemEval-S with a frontier reader (measured on v0.26.1), local semantic recall scored 85.8% against 72.2% without embeddings; this release enables local semantic recall by default when the companion is installed, except where embeddings are disabled or the small-host limit applies.
- **Embedding catch-up on large stores is on by default with local embeddings:** background catch-up no longer rescans already-embedded messages on every pass, and stays correct when messages arrive mid-run, when the chunking policy changes, or after a rollback. `/lcm status` reports failures per database and shows in-flight work separately. Exact semantic recall over large chunk stores loads only the selected chunks. On the same 250,000-row fully embedded store, recall in this release was no slower than in v0.28.1 over 800 recalls (400 per version) at the release candidate; 4 of the 400 rc2 recalls had no semantic coverage. This does not measure small-host or field latency ([#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586), [PR #1746](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1746), [PR #1758](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1758), [PR #1802](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1802), [PR #1821](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1821), [PR #1843](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1843), [PR #1860](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1860), [PR #1873](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1873), [PR #1893](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1893), [PR #1903](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1903)).
- **Sender label on gateway messages.** For gateway turns (Telegram, Discord and similar), LCM-X records the sender's platform user ID, for example `telegram:12345`, on the stored user message. It is an unverified label: it is not used for access control and does not change any stored or delivered text. CLI turns record nothing. Older rows are not filled in. Turn it off with `LCM_SENDER_CAPTURE=0` ([#995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/995), [PR #1875](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1875)).
- **Compaction pause survives restarts.** When an ordinary compaction pass finishes and changes nothing, LCM-X now records that in the session's metadata (`compaction_no_progress:v1:…`), so a restarted engine that receives the identical history skips the same no-op pass. The record holds only while nothing new is stored anywhere in the store; see **Known issues**. Forced, overflow, recovery and survival-ceiling compactions never wait ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #1888](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1888)).
- **Recall response fields.** Results can now include `duplicate_store_ids` (other exact copies of a hit) and `time_uncertain: carried` (the stored time may not be when the message was said). Both are described below.
- **One INFO log line per session end.** `LCM attribution phase=session_end …` gives the end reason, row and cursor counts and step timings. It never includes message content. The timings overlap; do not add them up ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #1906](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1906)).

Everything else under **Changes** is also on by default with no new setting, unless it is listed under **Optional features**.

## Upgrade

- **Host:** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is still required (0.21.5 or newer recommended), with Python 3.11 or newer. CI now also runs against the latest upstream Hermes as an advisory check only; that does not make upstream Hermes a supported host ([#1919](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1919), [PR #1921](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1921)).
- **Store:** the schema version stays 5. Two empty columns are added to the messages table (`sender_id`, `sender_source`). v0.28.1 ignores them, and rows it writes leave them empty ([PR #1875](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1875)).
- **Optional entity tables:** only when you set `LCM_ENTITIES_ENABLED=1`. The first start with it on creates six tables (`lcm_entities`, `lcm_entity_aliases`, `lcm_entity_keys`, `lcm_memory_notes`, `lcm_memory_events`, `lcm_memory_host_file_revisions`), three indexes and two triggers that keep the event log append-only, and turns on the `lcm_memory` lookup/list tool. Turning the setting off keeps the tables. v0.28.1 leaves them untouched ([#1862](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1862), [PR #1915](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1915)).
- **Chunk embedding triggers:** whenever local embeddings are on (now the default; opt out with `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false`). On the first chunk-store open after upgrade, LCM-X adds three triggers (two on the chunk metadata table, one on `messages`) and clears its coverage records once, so the next catch-up does a one-time rescan. A store that never used embeddings also gets the embedding and chunk tables that v0.28.1 already defines; no new table types are added. After a rollback to v0.28.1 the triggers stay in the database and SQLite keeps running them ([#1748](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1748), [PR #1758](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1758), [PR #1843](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1843)).
- **Local semantic recall turns on at upgrade** unless you set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false` (a blank or unrecognized value also turns it off; `true` keeps it on, including on small hosts). Install the companion when the installer offers it, or recall keeps using full text and `lcm_doctor` says so. On an existing store, the first start begins a one-time background catch-up. On hosts with 2 or fewer effective CPUs, the default skips semantic recall and answers from full text; set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true` explicitly to use it there anyway.
- **Rollback:** target `v0.28.1`. Take a SQLite-safe backup first, and compare ordered raw messages and summary provenance through upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade. Rollback with the sender columns and populated entity tables is covered by automated compatibility tests.
- **If you ran v0.29.0-rc1 with embedding prefixes:** after a rollback to v0.28.1 an older reader could pick up vectors made with a query/document prefix, compare unprefixed queries against them and write unprefixed vectors that survived re-upgrade. Prefixed vectors now use their own task names (`summary+prefix`, `chunk+prefix`), which v0.28.1 ignores. Stores without a prefix are unchanged ([#1942](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1942), [PR #1945](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1945)).
- **Deprecated settings:** `LCM_CACHE_FRIENDLY_CONDENSATION_ENABLED` and `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_TRANSCRIPT_GC_ENABLED` still work (off by default) and still warn in `/lcm status`, `lcm_status` and `lcm_doctor`. The v0.28.1 notes said they would be removed in v0.29.0; removal now happens in v0.30.0, and the warning text says so ([PR #1932](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1932)).

## Changes since v0.28.1

### Local semantic recall and install

- **Local semantic recall is on by default.** LCM-X now uses on-device embeddings (fastembed with `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`) out of the box; nothing leaves the machine. The dependency comes from the companion plugin `hermes-lcm-x-local-embeddings`, which `scripts/install.sh` offers. Until the companion, the model and the index are ready, recall answers from full-text search as before and reports `degraded=true` with the reason. Model preparation and the one-time catch-up over existing history run in the background; a recall can start preparation that may download the model, but queries never wait for a model download or backfill. `lcm_doctor` shows model readiness separately from index coverage, and names the exact enable command when the companion is missing. To opt out, set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false`. Explicit provider and model settings, cloud consent, and the missing-model check for cloud providers are unchanged for environment settings and new config objects (one Python-only exception is under **Known issues**) ([#1186](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1186), [PR #1956](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1956)).
- **Local embeddings install as a companion plugin.** The local-embedding dependency (fastembed) now ships in a separate companion plugin, `hermes-lcm-x-local-embeddings`, which the host installs with its own consent prompt. LCM-X itself still has no Python dependencies, so declining or failing that install never disables memory: full-text recall keeps working, and the installer prints the exact command to retry. The installer now also targets the right profile when `HERMES_PROFILE` is set or `HERMES_HOME` points at a profile directory, and refuses a conflicting pair before changing anything ([#1186](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1186), [PR #1940](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1940)).
- **Small hosts adapt instead of timing out.** When local embeddings are on by default and the host has at most 2 effective CPUs (affinity, cgroup quota and host capacity are all checked), recall answers from full-text search right away and reports `degraded=true` with reason `cpu_limited` and the real coverage of each arm. Set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true` to use semantic recall on a small host; setting only `LCM_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=fastembed` does not bypass this limit. Background catch-up still runs ([#1186](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1186), [#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586), [PR #1938](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1938)).
- **Scanner-clean install payload for the plugin catalog.** Each release tag now also publishes a runtime-only copy of the plugin: its import closure plus `plugin.yaml`, `LICENSE` and the bundled skill, built from the tag's exact commit. It is published as a new commit on the `dist` branch (under `plugin/`), with a manifest attached to the release. Current Hermes scans a plugin's whole tree before install, and this payload passes that scan where the full repository does not. The v0.28.1 payload is published, and a catalog update to it has been proposed upstream ([#1946](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1946), [PR #1958](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1958)).

### Recall and search

- **Matches deep in long messages:** recall now returns up to its full 25 matches when the match sits deep in a long message, each with an exact quote; before, only the first 8 came back. This covers CJK and emoji text and the fallback search path. Ranking and response limits are unchanged ([#1678](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1678), [#1685](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1685), [PR #1679](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1679), [PR #1703](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1703)).
- **Duplicate hits counted once:** exact stored copies of a message (same session, role, tool call, content and recorded time) count once against recall and grep limits. The best-ranked copy is shown; the others are listed in `duplicate_store_ids`. Copies with no recorded time, or different times, stay separate. Stored rows, raw reads and `lcm_expand` are unchanged ([#1681](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1681), [PR #1683](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1683)).
- **Identifiers and broad searches:** a search for an identifier such as `VALUE_S1586_SHARD000007_0000` matches the exact identifier first and broadens only when nothing matches. Broad searches on large stores, and session and vector loading, do less work. Result order and limits are unchanged; no general speed guarantee is claimed ([#1749](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1749), [PR #1745](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1745), [PR #1750](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1750), [PR #1757](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1757)).
- **Media captions are searchable:** newly stored media placeholders keep a short text preview of the caption. Media bytes are not stored in the preview, and older rows are not filled in ([#1702](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1702), [#1718](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1718), [PR #1710](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1710), [PR #1720](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1720)).

### Retries, stopped turns and restarts

- **Retried tool turns:** when a turn is retried after its tool output was pruned, each new message and tool call/result is stored once, both while running and after a restart. Some cold-restart retry shapes are still open (see **Known issues**) ([#1540](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1540), [PR #1830](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1830)).
- **Compaction records are written atomically:** compaction saves its record of which messages it covered in a single database write, so a crash can no longer leave a half-written record that later drops or duplicates a message ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451), [PR #1882](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1882)).
- **Re-sent messages after a restart:** a user message re-sent in the same position with the same text and a later timestamp is now stored instead of dropped. If the host only re-timestamps a message and nothing else tells it apart from a real resend, it may still be stored twice ([#1511](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1511), [#1328](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1328), [PR #1780](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1780), [PR #1810](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1810)).
- **Failed reads retry:** if a database read fails at session start or during an identity check, the next turn retries instead of skipping messages or storing them twice. Before, an edited earlier message could be skipped for good ([#1317](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1317), [#1353](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1353), [PR #1803](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1803), [PR #1807](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1807)).
- **Re-examined messages follow your rules:** when LCM-X re-examines earlier messages, they go through your ignore patterns and large-output rules again, and only those messages are re-checked ([#1628](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1628), [#1822](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1822), [PR #1816](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1816), [PR #1874](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1874)).
- **Stopped turns are saved right away:** a turn you stop after the assistant or a tool has produced output is saved immediately instead of on the next turn. A turn stopped before any reply, or right after a reset, is still saved on the next turn ([#1623](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1623), [PR #1806](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1806)).
- **Two connections, one session:** binding and finishing a session no longer overwrite another connection's live state, and empty-session cleanup no longer removes an engine running in the same process ([#634](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/634), [#753](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/753), [PR #730](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/730), [PR #762](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/762)).
- **Simultaneous opens:** two engines or a maintenance worker opening the same store at once no longer fail with "index already exists" or "trigger already exists" errors ([#1744](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1744), [#1771](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1771), [PR #1747](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1747), [PR #1778](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1778)).

### Compaction and diagnostics

- **Summaries ending with a doubled closer are kept.** Some small summary models end a valid summary with `</lcm-summary>` twice. LCM-X treated the second one as the last line and discarded the summary (logged as `reason=no_content`), so the backlog stayed uncompacted until a retry happened to succeed. A run of identical closers at the very end now counts as one and is logged as `tolerated repeated_closer`. Thanks to the community contributor who found and fixed this ([#1948](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1948), [PR #1949](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1949)).
- **Less redundant work:** below the compaction threshold, LCM-X no longer asks the host to rebuild its prompt only to swap large tool outputs for stubs; the swap waits for the next real compaction. Redaction, quarantine and ignore cleanups still apply immediately ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #1887](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1887)). The restart-proof pause is described above.
- **Store-wedge inspector:** a new read-only operator tool, `scripts/store_wedge_inspect.py`, reads a stopped copy of a store and reports why compaction is stuck, or `unknown` when it cannot tell. It never repairs anything. Steps are in `docs/operations/store-wedge-inspect.md`, and the doctor's compaction-progress warning links there ([#1598](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1598), [#1162](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1162), [PR #1737](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1737), [PR #1752](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1752), [PR #1786](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1786)).
- **Duplicate-check diagnostics:** the message-ID observer (shadow mode) also counts conflicts that differ only in whitespace. Matching and stored data are unchanged ([#1787](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1787), [PR #1808](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1808)).

### Dates, evidence and configuration

- **Uncertain times are flagged:** when a message's stored time may not be when it was said (for example after an edit or a resend), recall and the evidence tools (`lcm_evidence_pack`, `lcm_compile_evidence`, `lcm_compute`, `lcm_retrieve`) mark it `time_uncertain: carried`, list rows left out at a date cutoff, and do not compute exact date answers from them. Stored times are unchanged ([#1507](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1507), [#1779](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1779), [PR #1776](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1776), [PR #1794](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1794)).
- **Dates read the same way everywhere:** month names and mixed formats such as `2024/05-03` are read the same for every row. When a quote mixes dates from different events, LCM-X marks the day unknown instead of guessing, so some answers that used to carry a date no longer do. If the store cannot be read, automatic evidence compilation falls back with reason `store_unavailable` instead of an error. Automatic compilation itself stays off by default (`LCM_PREANSWER_EVIDENCE_ENABLED`) ([#1801](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1801), [#1811](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1811), [#1851](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1851), [PR #1804](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1804), [PR #1826](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1826), [PR #1858](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1858)).
- **config.yaml without PyYAML:** when PyYAML is missing (as on current upstream Hermes), LCM-X prefers `ruamel.yaml`, and its last-resort parser now keeps quoted strings and simple lists. `lcm.model_thresholds` values must be numbers: write `model: 0.35`, not a quoted number ([#1916](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1916), [PR #1918](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1918)).

## Optional features — off by default

- **Local (on-device) embeddings** moved out of this list: they are on by default from this release (see **Changes since v0.28.1**); `docs/embeddings-setup.md` covers the companion, model choice and opt-out.
- **Session-pack recall** (`LCM_RECALL_DELIVERY_UNIT=session`; default `hits`): delivers the messages around each ranked session in source order, keeping tool calls with their results, and now retries fitting groups it skipped for space ([#1188](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1188), [#1828](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1828), [PR #1695](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1695), [PR #1868](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1868)).
- **Entity memory, read-only** (`LCM_ENTITIES_ENABLED=1`): the `lcm_memory` tool's `lookup` and `list` return cited mentions of a person or thing across sessions, with labelled times. Facts from assertions also need `LCM_ASSERTIONS_ENABLED`. Merge, split, undo and forget are not exposed yet ([#1862](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1862), [PR #1865](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1865), [PR #1915](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1915), [PR #1920](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1920)).
- **Entity memory groundwork (off by default, not exposed yet):** internal links from stored facts' subjects to the right person per sender, with reversible corrections. No tool, turn-path or schema change ([#1862](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1862), [PR #1926](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1926)).
- **Embedding prefixes** (Ollama and OpenAI-compatible providers): add a separate text prefix to queries and to documents, for models that expect one, with `LCM_EMBEDDING_QUERY_PREFIX` / `LCM_EMBEDDING_DOCUMENT_PREFIX` or `lcm.embedding_query_prefix` / `lcm.embedding_document_prefix` in config.yaml (quote values to keep spaces; the environment variable wins). A prefix changes the vector identity, so restart Hermes before a warmup or backfill. Thanks to the community contributor who proposed this ([#1118](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1118), [PR #1911](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1911)).

## Testing improved

- **Real-host CI:** an advisory upstream-Hermes cell and config checks without PyYAML; changed tests must actually run (`tests-ran`), merge-group CI covers previously unselected tests, and a real-host failure of the `/new` stored-rows test uploads a content-free structural capture ([#1919](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1919), [PR #1921](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1921), [PR #1783](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1783), [PR #1784](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1784), [PR #1791](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1791), [PR #1793](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1793)).
- **Message-loss reliability checker:** false failures fixed. These are checker fixes, not new product results. The survival-fit deficits once reported on the oldest pinned host came from a scoring gap; with the corrected scorer both runs on that host pass ([#1799](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1799), [#1879](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1879), [PR #1800](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1800), [PR #1870](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1870), [PR #1892](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1892)).
- **Regression tests with every fix:** each recall, loader and date fix above ships with tests that pin payload, ordering and fallback behaviour. A steady-retry change made during this cycle (PR #1637) was reverted before release because it could drop sibling tool results; a regression test now guards that case ([#1636](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1636), [PR #1884](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1884)). The selected-batch chunk loader gains score-tolerance and archived-exclusion regressions ([#1901](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1901), [PR #1927](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1927)).
- **Upgrade and rollback tests:** the sender columns and the optional entity tables are tested against pinned older releases up to v0.28.1, and compatibility fixtures now use SQLite-safe backups that include WAL data ([#1909](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1909), [PR #1913](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1913), [PR #1105](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1105)).
- **Flaky tests made deterministic:** timing-sensitive tests now use explicit barriers, drains and logical clocks, and passing tests no longer keep their temporary stores ([#1923](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1923), [#1905](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1905), [PR #1925](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1925), [PR #1930](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1930), [PR #1690](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1690), [PR #1717](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1717), [PR #1835](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1835), [PR #1856](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1856)).
- **Measurement tools:** new probes for local embedding catch-up (speed, CPU, recall while catching up, integrity); the Frontier Measurement Protocol harness gains strict verdict parsing, paired run checks and speaker-label and session-date variants; release-gate comparison rules (D1/D4/D8) and the calibrated Track S rule get producers, scorers and bounded retries ([#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586), [#1189](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1189), [#1824](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1824), [PR #1751](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1751), [PR #1849](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1849), [PR #1866](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1866), [PR #1861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1861)).
- **Public results:** the results page, README highlights and plugin description now come from one sourced dataset with drift checks, each new scoreboard row is its own file, and the pending check rejects duplicate row IDs and supersession cycles ([#1885](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1885), [#1895](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1895), [PR #1785](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1785), [PR #1867](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1867), [PR #1886](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1886), [PR #1928](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1928)).
- **Release gauntlet instruments:** the D4 recall-health replacement step is a permanent, CI-collected tool that checks that both attempts used the same instrument and lists which fields it compared ([PR #1954](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1954)); the B4 drained-store coverage check accepts witnessed drained coverage and rejects ambiguous tail matches ([#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900), [PR #1952](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1952)); the Phase A host check runs in an isolated Hermes home and tells "preparing" from "prepared" ([#1941](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1941), [PR #1950](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1950), [PR #1947](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1947)).
- **Host suite:** fixed dependency and capability fixtures that made the host test suite fail for reasons unrelated to the product ([#1539](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1539), [PR #1951](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1951)).
- **Default-flip consent and benchmark cells:** every way of copying a config (`dataclasses.replace`, asdict/JSON, pickle, copy, and a reset to omitted) is tested for cloud consent against recorded HTTP calls with sockets refused. The benchmark producers (QA bridge and LongMemEval) are tested to certify LOCAL coverage before scoring, so a LOCAL row can no longer silently measure full-text recall ([PR #1956](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1956)).
- **Companion and small-host cells:** decline, noninteractive and profile-targeting installs are tested against exact host pins; the CPU detector is tested on affinity, cgroup v1/v2 and malformed inputs; a v0.28.1 rollback test reproduces the prefix contamination before the fix.

## Known issues

- **Repeated compaction passes on long sessions that cannot shrink** ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [#1162](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1162)): when a session's history cannot be cut before an unresolved retained occurrence, each pass makes no progress. In this release the 10-minute pause after such a pass ends as soon as any new message is stored, so the next turn can run another 10–73 s pass; v0.28.1 waited the full 10 minutes. Nothing is lost. v0.29.1 restores the 10-minute pause ([PR #2002](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2002)), and a planned fix lets compaction get past such a row by summarising it from the stored copy ([PR #2003](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2003)). The live copy stays in context, so its content is duplicated, never lost.
- **Slow summaries can shrink the live view:** when summary calls time out at the compaction threshold, the survival fit can drop about 80–115 older rows from what the model sees. The store keeps every row and recall can still reach them; a fix is tracked for v0.31.0 ([#2004](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2004)).
- **Catalog install on upstream Hermes with the plugin scanner:** the catalog entry still pins the full repository, which current Hermes rates `dangerous` and refuses to install. A catalog update to the scanner-clean payload is proposed upstream; until it lands, use `scripts/install.sh` on those hosts. This release's payload is rated `caution` (not `safe`) because the small-host CPU detector reads `/proc`; nothing was changed to hide that from the scanner, and an upstream allowance is requested ([#1946](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1946)). Hermes 0.21.3's scanner blocks a `caution` verdict from a community source, so a catalog install there needs `--force` after reviewing the findings, or `scripts/install.sh`.
- **Upstream Hermes manual `/compress`:** on current upstream Hermes main, a manual `/compress` from the gateway uses the host's own compressor and bypasses LCM-X, so stored history can gain duplicate replies. No rows were lost in the reported cases. A fix is proposed upstream ([Hermes #143587](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143587)); an LCM-X defence is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1922](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1922), [#1924](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1924)).
- **Retry shapes still being fixed** (all are redesigned together for v0.30.0, including the two cases that can lose a row, #1837 and #1838):
  - after a tool call is retried with new message IDs, each later cold restart can store that call and its result again: one more copy per restart, nothing lost ([#1836](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1836));
  - after a cold restart, if only the tool result's message ID changes on a retry, the new result may not be stored ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837));
  - if the plugin restarts before a session's first compaction and the host re-sends the last tool turn with a new timestamp, that turn may not be stored ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838));
  - in some retry and restart sequences after compaction, a replaced or retried message can be dropped or stored twice ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
  Real-host frequency is unknown.
- **A re-stamped tool turn after a cold restart (found in engine tests, new in v0.29.0):** after compaction and a cold restart, if a host that gives messages no unique IDs re-sends the last assistant/tool pair with new timestamps while the user message before it keeps its own, LCM-X can bind the pair to the stored copy as a retry and not store it. A trace of the supported Hermes hosts found no path that produces this sequence; it was reproduced only in an engine-level test. The fix refuses that binding when the pair's own timestamps differ, mirroring the existing message-ID check; it is merged on main, and the issue is tracked for v0.30.0 ([#1967](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1967), [PR #1969](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1969)).
- **Crash before a reply, then rotation:** on hosts that do not give messages unique IDs, if the agent crashes before replying and the conversation then rotates, the next turn can be stored twice. The v0.28.1 notes planned this fix for v0.29.0; it now targets v0.30.0 ([#1508](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1508)).
- **Duplicates kept on purpose:** turns stored before this release's carried-stamp marker can be stored again by a replay, and user messages that the host itself mirrors after an ACP crash recovery are kept twice. LCM-X keeps both copies rather than risk losing a genuine message; see `docs/identity-ledger.md` ([#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501), [PR #1775](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1775)).
- **Replays can store rows a second time:** when a host replays rows that carry no timestamps, tool results and replies that are already stored can be stored again, as on v0.28.x. Nothing is lost, but recall can show the row twice; a fix is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A crash right after a rotation can keep an extra reply:** after such a crash, LCM-X can store an assistant reply that the host never made durable, so it holds one reply more than the host. Nothing is lost; this shape predates v0.29.0 and appeared intermittently in one reliability cell ([#824](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/824), [#861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/861)).
- **Local embeddings on large, fully embedded stores (small hosts):** on a 2-CPU host with a 250,000-row fully embedded store, a semantic recall could use its full 8-second budget. In this release, hosts with at most 2 effective CPUs answer from full text immediately when local embeddings are on by default (`degraded=true`, `cpu_limited`); explicit settings keep control. Faster exact semantic recall under contention is tracked in [#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586); the first attempt did not meet its memory bar, so no release is promised yet.
- **Local embeddings can outvote exact keyword hits:** with the deep-match fix above, recall with embeddings off now returns its full 25 matches as well, and on the LoCoMo benchmark it answers more questions than the default local embeddings (1,165 vs 1,089 of 1,986 questions). Fusion gives the keyword arm half the weight of each embedding arm, so embedding-only hits can push an exact keyword hit out of the 25. Local embeddings still lead on LongMemEval-S (426 vs 408 of 500) and show no regression against v0.28.1. A fusion-weight fix is planned for a v0.29.x patch ([#950](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/950)).
- **Python only: switching an existing config object to a cloud provider:** if code changes `embedding_provider` to a cloud provider on an `LCMConfig` that already resolved to the local default (with `dataclasses.replace` or attribute assignment), the enabled setting carries over, and that provider starts receiving text without `embeddings_enabled=True`. Settings from the environment and new `LCMConfig(...)` objects are not affected. Set `embeddings_enabled` explicitly when you switch providers in code; a fix is tracked in [#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959).
- **Subagent work is not stored:** what a delegated subagent does in its own session, including its tool calls and intermediate results, is not stored by LCM-X. Only what the subagent returns to the parent conversation is stored, so `lcm_recall` cannot find a subagent's intermediate results. This isolation is not new in this release. Storing subagent sessions is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1931](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931)).
- **Cross-process cleanup:** another process sharing the store can still clear an empty live session binding and stall later compaction ([#753](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/753), [#761](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/761)).
- **Extra rows in one degraded mode:** when a child compaction can never publish, three runtime hosts store extra rows and repeat user tags. No user content is missing. That reliability cell now gates on missing content only ([#1797](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1797), [#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900), [PR #1929](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1929)).
- **Summary input order after a host reorder ([#2007](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2007)).** When the host moves a stored row later in its view, the rows given to the summariser for one leaf can be out of store order, so an older fact can follow its correction inside a summary. Stored rows are not reordered, dropped or duplicated. Found during this release's review; the fix is planned for v0.29.1.

For 2 of them, the reviewed head differs from the landed head only by merges from main or markdown-only commits. Source: GitHub review records; this says nothing about review depth.

- **Full suite on pinned Hermes hosts** (run 40160319195): the raw result FAILED on all 7 hosts, with 29 to 42 failures out of 22,419 tests per host.

Not green under the written gate, because tracked issues for the 65 are not named (decision below).

- **Phase C (7 real hosts): one bar, doctor clean, is not green; every other bar passes on all 7.**
  - 0 LOSS on every host.

  - The re-paste after restart passes on all 7.
  - 0 publication-invariant conflicts.

No disposition covers the other two, and v0.28.1 did not report them (its embeddings check passed, with embeddings off by default), so none is available at this release (decision below).

  - D1 recall scorecard (OFF): PASS. LongMemEval-M, 500 questions per tree: 0 recall flips and 0 full-text flips against v0.28.1, recall@10 0.873 on both trees, 0 unhealthy questions, and 0 A/A′ row or rank discordance on either tree.
  - D1 LOCAL was not run, so this gating row is not green: as written, it embeds each question's full history with the cache off, more than 100 hours in total. At this release, local recall rests on D4 LOCAL, the #1586 same-store row and the Phase C LOCAL cells (D8 LOCAL is recorded, but its placebo is invalid). Making D1 LOCAL fit a release window is [#1971](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1971).
  - D2/D3 Track S facts kept: not green. Its base-against-base placebo run failed its own bar because of two provider-latency events: in each, a summary call ran close to the 120 s timeout (one timed out), and the fit then dropped live rows ([#2004](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2004)). Both arms ran the same build, so this measures the instrument, not the release. The fix is a predeclared rule that treats a summariser timeout as a service fault, and it applies from v0.29.1. Compactions per 100 turns: 15.6 (bar 25). Mean turn wait: 5.5 s (bar 15 s). Waited-turn share: 15.6% (bar 25%). Wall p90: 39.4 s (bar 120 s; max 69.6 s). 0 dropped rows, 0 timeouts, 0 failures. D5-B store-clone cells: two bars are not green. The cells are 2 fresh stores on a pinned copy of the reference agent's Hermes v0.22.2 host. They use a sanitized snapshot of its LCM settings instead of a live profile read, with summaries on glm-5.3 in a 128k test window, the context threshold at 0.5 with 8,000-token leaf chunks so compaction runs within 44 turns, and the agent's per-model threshold entry dropped; they are labelled degraded full text. 0 missing and 0 duplicated rows; restart, re-paste and all probes pass, and the largest compaction attempt was 61.9 s (bar 145 s). The doctor result, saved by reference, has 20 checks with 0 failed and 3 warnings, but the reader missed it (raw INCONCLUSIVE). Each cell has 7 host-caught detach tracebacks with an LCM-X frame against a bar of 0 (raw FAIL), one per detach attempt, as on v0.28.1. The previous-GA dispositions for both are unavailable at this release (decision below).
  - D4 recall QA, paired v0.28.1 vs rc2, OFF (product defaults, embeddings off): PASS on both datasets. LongMemEval-S: 379 → 408 of 500 (paired 8 / 37, exact McNemar p 1.5e-05). LoCoMo: 1,012 → 1,165 of 1,986 (57 / 210, p 9e-22). No LongMemEval-S question type went down (the 30 abstention questions were net 2 lower). On LoCoMo the adversarial category went from 210 to 204 of 446 (−1.3 points) and every other category went up. The A/A′ placebo was accepted on both trees (LongMemEval-S fixed 100: 2 and 3 discordant; LoCoMo: 70 and 81 of 1,986). Reader and judge calls that completed after a network reconnect were kept and are disclosed in the receipt; counting every one of them against rc2 leaves both verdicts unchanged. rc2 hands the reader more recalled context: +33% reader input tokens on LongMemEval-S and +17% on LoCoMo.
  - D4 recall QA, paired v0.28.1 vs rc2, LOCAL (local embeddings on): PASS on both datasets, neutral release over release. LongMemEval-S: 425 → 426 of 500 (paired 3 / 4, exact McNemar p 1.0). LoCoMo: 1,083 → 1,089 of 1,986 (37 / 43, p 0.58). Category moves are within a few questions either way (largest: LoCoMo adversarial +6, temporal +4, multi-hop −2). The A/A′ placebo was accepted on both trees (LongMemEval-S fixed 100: 1 and 1 discordant; LoCoMo: 72 and 88 of 1,986). Counting every reconnect-recovered call against rc2 leaves both verdicts unchanged. Reader input tokens are unchanged (±0.1%): with embeddings on, both versions already return full recall results.
  - D8 per-category non-inferiority is not green. The written gate makes D8 a gating row from this release, the one that turns local recall on by default. With local embeddings it passes on both datasets; with embeddings off it does not (lowest bounds: abstention on LongMemEval-S, 30 questions; adversarial on LoCoMo). But the A/A′ placebo fails on all four rows, so the row is invalid, and it was not re-run. The release ships by a release-manager decision (below), and the placebo bar is being reworked before D8 can pass.
- **Agentic check ([#995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/995)):** PASS under both pre-declared judges. On 1,682 held-out LoCoMo questions answered by agent-driven recall with local embeddings, storing speaker names and dates with each message raised accuracy from 79.5% to 85.3% (Sol judge; GLM judge 76.9% to 83.0%), exact paired McNemar p < 1e-11 under both judges. The whole gain is in the adversarial category (+25.4 and +27.8 points); categories 1-4 are unchanged (p 0.72 and 1.0), so there is no loss elsewhere. Judge agreement on the speaker-name arm was κ 0.82, below the 0.85 agreement bar, so the result is recorded as judge-sensitive. It was measured on main at 238d1a9e, before the rc2 tag, and was not re-run on the rc2 tree. It measures speaker provenance in stored text on the benchmark adapter; the sender label this release records on gateway messages is not yet delivered to the reader.
- **Reference-agent window (≥24 h on the exact rc2 tree; window restarted 2026-10-26 05:24Z after an unrelated host update):** not green under the written gate (raw reader verdict FAIL, and the compaction-activity bar is not met: no published organic compaction and no synthetic top-up); its failure classes pass with dispositions over 31.3 h. The strict integrity read fails, and every failure class already existed on v0.28.x:
  - Delegated sub-agent sessions are not stored on this host ([#1931](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931), v0.30.0).
  - Replays store rows a second time ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674), v0.30.0). In the window, the replay bursts are the same size as before it.
  - Detach traces on background-review sessions are caught by the host.
  - Doctor warnings were already present before the window.
  - Large image tool results that the host later replaced with a placeholder are kept in full by LCM-X.
  - No organic compaction happened in the window, and no synthetic top-up ran. For a minor release the written gate requires one of the two, so the window's compaction-activity bar is not met. By a release-manager decision (below), compaction on this release rests on Phase C, D5-B and D7.
- **[#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501):** strict raw verdict FAIL on the rc2 tree, against v0.28.1 on the same instrument: 12 cell pairs, 7 PASS, 2 FAIL, 3 UNSUPPORTED. The 2 failing pairs are the two crash-after-rotation duplicate shapes that the earlier #1501 ruling retained (one in-process upgrade cell, one ACP cell; see docs/identity-ledger.md): one key-based duplicate row on both v0.28.1 and rc2, 0 missing, 0 excess, and every supported ordered projection equal to v0.28.1. No new regression. Disposition: pre-existing, accepted tradeoff, non-blocking. The 3 ACP upgrade cells are unsupported by the harness and recorded, not counted as failures.

**Release-manager decisions.**
- #1967 is engine-level only and disclosed above; its fix (PR #1969) is merged on main and the issue is tracked for v0.30.0.
- D1 LOCAL was deferred (above).
- Seven rows are not green under the written gate, and the release ships anyway: D1 LOCAL (not run), D2/D3 (its placebo run failed), D8 (its placebo is invalid on every row, including base against base where it was read, so it measures the instrument), the reference-agent window (no organic compaction or synthetic top-up), the Phase C doctor bar, the D5-B doctor and traceback bars, and the Phase B host suites and reliability matrix. For the last three, the previous-GA dispositions are unavailable. The kit did not record some of the evidence they need: full previous-GA doctor results on six Phase C hosts, counts per triggering host event, and a tracked issue for each pre-existing failure. Some warnings also have no matching previous-GA shape. The spec rows give the reasons host by host. Neither the Phase C nor the D5-B gap shows a lost, duplicated or reordered stored row, or a failed doctor check. The reliability-matrix failures include missing-row and duplicate-row shapes that v0.28.1 also shows, plus the known intermittent #861. The v0.29.1 gauntlet runs each again; each must pass or carry a new disclosed decision. The decisions are recorded in the release spec ([PR #2006](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2006)).
- The test kit gained an isolated home for every test process. The D4 reader keeps its own sign-in through a reader-only route. Instrument changes only; no product change.
- D2/D3 facts kept is not green (above); facts kept rests on D7. From v0.29.1 a replay with a summariser timeout is service-invalid and is re-run once.
- Two test-harness defects were found and fixed during the run, each tested both ways before reuse:
  - the Phase C proof script did not follow a doctor result saved by reference;
  - the store-clone runner's environment isolation conflicted with its own preflight guard, so earlier store-clone launches stopped before their cells.
  Neither changed a product result.
- Fixes for [#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880) and the [#1162](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1162) escape path are planned for v0.29.1, and #1967 is tracked for v0.30.0. The local-embeddings keyword weighting ([#950](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/950)) follows in a v0.29.x patch.
